prep.text: Area, sponsor and team leader chosen; the event is in the site plan
Charter agreed with the sponsor: scope, goals, boundaries, budget
Baseline data collected: volumes, cycle times, defects, WIP
Team chosen and invited: operators from the area, support functions, fresh eyes
Operators released from production: cover planned for every day of the event
Area informed: all shifts, the areas up- and downstream, the works council where needed
Current-state data ready: layout drawing, standard work, a video of the process
Materials and tools ready: room, stopwatches, tape and labels, flip charts, maintenance and IT on call
Report-out booked with the sponsor and the area for the last day

agenda.title: Training and current state
items: Kick-off: the sponsor opens, the team reads the charter
Lean basics: the 8 wastes, flow, standard work
Walk the process from the start to the end of the scope
Time every step: at least 10 cycles each
Draw the spaghetti diagram of the operator's walk
List the waste you saw, step by step
Agree the baseline of every goal

agenda.title: Analyse and generate ideas
items: Compare the cycle times with the takt time
Find the root causes of the biggest waste (5 Whys, fishbone)
Collect ideas from every team member, the operators first
Place each idea on effort and impact
Choose what to try first and start the Kaizen newspaper

agenda.title: Try and implement
items: Try the first changes on the floor, with the operators
Move tools and material to the point of use
Measure each trial: keep what works, change what does not
Check the safety and ergonomics of every change
Give every newspaper item an owner and a date

agenda.title: Standardise and measure
items: Write the new standard work with the operators
Train the operators of every shift who will run it
Measure every goal on the new process
5S the area: labels, floor markings, shadow boards
Agree the 30-day follow-up list with owners and dates

agenda.title: Report out
items: Measure the goals once more on the running process
Prepare the report-out: before and after, what changed
Report out to the sponsor and the area, the operators presenting
Hand the follow-up list to the area owner
Recognise the team

fields.name: e.g. Packing line 2: walk less, pack faster
fields.scopeStart: e.g. Tote arrives at the packing bench
fields.scopeEnd: e.g. Labelled parcel on the outbound conveyor
fields.problem: What is wrong today, in numbers, and who feels it
fields.whyNow: e.g. Peak season in eight weeks; agency hours over budget
fields.outOfBounds: e.g. No new conveyor, no change to the WMS, no change to shift times
fields.changed: The changes in a few lines, as the operators would say them

tips: Most of an event's result is decided in the weeks before it: a narrow scope, measurable goals, the data, and operators really free from production.
The people who do the work are the team.
At least one operator from the area, better a third of the team. Add a support function and one pair of fresh eyes from another area.
Day one is on the floor: walk it, time it, draw the walk. Ideas come on day two, trials on day three, while the team is still together.
Measure before and after the same way.
Same metric, same unit, same method. The tool says for each goal whether lower or higher is better, so the change is never read the wrong way round.
What is not finished in the event goes on the follow-up list with an owner and a date. The 30-day check is when the area shows the sponsor that the gains held.

example.name: Packing line 2: walk less, pack faster
example.scopeStart: Tote arrives at the packing bench
example.scopeEnd: Labelled parcel on the outbound conveyor
example.problem: Packers walk 18.4 m per parcel to fetch cartons, tape and labels from the shared printer; a parcel takes 96 s, and 42 totes wait at the benches at peak. The late shift needs agency staff every day to clear the volume.
example.whyNow: Peak season starts in eight weeks with 30% more volume; agency hours are 18% over budget.
example.outOfBounds: No new conveyor, no change to the WMS, no change to shift times or the number of benches.
example.savingsNote: One agency post of 8.8 paid hours a day less on 250 days: 2,200 hours at €28.
example.changed: Cartons, tape and labels at every bench. Totes roll to the packer on a gravity lane of four. Five carton sizes instead of nine. A two-bin carton supply refilled by the water spider. The second weight scan is gone.

ideas.text: Cartons, tape and void fill at every bench, at the point of use
Gravity lane of four totes in front of each bench, first in first out
Limit the totes waiting per bench to four, lane marked on the floor
Five carton sizes at the bench instead of nine
Two-bin carton supply, refilled by the water spider
Idea cards at every bench, read at the start of the shift
A label printer at every bench, printing on the last scan
Remove the second weight scan after the quality sign-off
Repair the conveyor merge that jams at peak
Train the late and night shifts on the new standard work
Water spider round every 45 minutes instead of 60
Height-adjustable tables for all eight benches
Release the orders to picking sorted by carton size
